Artist Lucy Smith created the [Analemma Project](https://artlucy.uk/index.php/the-analemma-project/) sculpture. She completed her PhD "Making the Conceptual Tangible: The Role of Art in Communicating Science" here at the University of Dundee.

The [Analemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analemma) is an unequal figure-of-eight shape, created by tracking the sun's position in the sky at the same time each day over a period of one year.

## Why doesn't the Earth fall onto the Sun?

The Analemma traces that figure-of-eight because the Earth's orbit isn't a perfect circle travelled at constant speed -- it's an ellipse, and Earth moves faster when it's closer to the Sun. Working out exactly *why* orbits look like this took the better part of three centuries. **Galileo** discovered  that not everything orbits the Earth; **Kepler**,  worked out the precise shape of orbit based on observations; **Newton** explained *why*  from a single law of gravity; and **Einstein**'s' general relativity is needed to explain a tiny mismatch between Newton's theory and Mercury's orbit.

::: {.content-hidden when-format="pdf"}

## Simulating a planet orbiting the sun?

In the app below change the initial speed and direction of the orbiting object. Can you find conditions for which the planet crashes into the sun rather than stay in an eliiptical orbit? 

::: {#fig-newton-gravity .content-hidden when-format="pdf"}

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  if (window.SHOW_JS_APPS === false) return;

  var GM_SUN = 4 * Math.PI * Math.PI; // AU^3/year^2 -- makes Earth's orbit (a=1 AU) have a 1-year period
  var R_START = 1.0;   // AU, fixed starting distance from the Sun
  var R_CRASH = 0.10;  // AU, an enlarged "you've hit the Sun" radius, purely so a crash is visible
  var V_CIRC = Math.sqrt(GM_SUN / R_START);

  function initialState(speedFactor, angleDeg) {
    var speed = speedFactor * V_CIRC;
    var theta = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180;
    return [R_START, 0.0, speed * Math.sin(theta), speed * Math.cos(theta)];
  }

  // Classify the orbit from its initial conditions alone (energy and
  // angular momentum) -- exact, not an approximation.
  function classifyOrbit(x0, y0, vx0, vy0) {
    var r0 = Math.hypot(x0, y0);
    var v0sq = vx0 * vx0 + vy0 * vy0;
    var energy = 0.5 * v0sq - GM_SUN / r0;
    var L = x0 * vy0 - y0 * vx0;
    var info = { energy: energy, L: L, bound: energy < 0 };
    if (energy < 0) {
      var a = -GM_SUN / (2 * energy);
      var eSq = Math.max(0.0, 1 - (L * L) / (GM_SUN * a));
      var e = Math.sqrt(eSq);
      info.a = a; info.e = e;
      info.period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(Math.pow(a, 3) / GM_SUN);
      info.periapsis = a * (1 - e);
      info.apoapsis = a * (1 + e);
    }
    return info;
  }

  // Velocity-Verlet integration of F = -GM/r^2, with an adaptive step size
  // proportional to the local orbital timescale (~r^1.5), fine near the
  // Sun and coarse far away.
  function simulateNewtonOrbit(x0, y0, vx0, vy0, maxTime, maxSteps, rCrash, eta) {
    maxSteps = maxSteps || 6000;
    rCrash = (rCrash === undefined) ? R_CRASH : rCrash;
    eta = eta || 0.01;
    var xs = [x0], ys = [y0], ts = [0.0];
    var x = x0, y = y0, vx = vx0, vy = vy0, t = 0.0, crashed = false;
    for (var s = 0; s < maxSteps; s++) {
      var r = Math.hypot(x, y);
      if (r < rCrash) { crashed = true; break; }
      var dt = eta * Math.pow(r, 1.5) / Math.sqrt(GM_SUN);
      dt = Math.min(dt, maxTime / 40.0);
      var ax = -GM_SUN * x / Math.pow(r, 3);
      var ay = -GM_SUN * y / Math.pow(r, 3);
      var vxh = vx + 0.5 * ax * dt;
      var vyh = vy + 0.5 * ay * dt;
      x = x + vxh * dt; y = y + vyh * dt; t += dt;
      var r2 = Math.hypot(x, y);
      if (r2 < rCrash) { crashed = true; xs.push(x); ys.push(y); ts.push(t); break; }
      var ax2 = -GM_SUN * x / Math.pow(r2, 3);
      var ay2 = -GM_SUN * y / Math.pow(r2, 3);
      vx = vxh + 0.5 * ax2 * dt; vy = vyh + 0.5 * ay2 * dt;
      xs.push(x); ys.push(y); ts.push(t);
      if (t >= maxTime) break;
    }
    return { xs: xs, ys: ys, ts: ts, crashed: crashed };
  }

  function runNewtonSim(speedFactor, angleDeg) {
    var s0 = initialState(speedFactor, angleDeg);
    var info = classifyOrbit(s0[0], s0[1], s0[2], s0[3]);
    var maxTime = info.bound ? Math.min(3 * info.period, 15.0) : 4.0;
    var sim = simulateNewtonOrbit(s0[0], s0[1], s0[2], s0[3], maxTime);
    info.crashed = sim.crashed; info.xs = sim.xs; info.ys = sim.ys; info.ts = sim.ts;
    return info;
  }

  function interpPosition(t, ts, xs, ys) {
    var n = ts.length;
    if (t <= ts[0]) return [xs[0], ys[0]];
    if (t >= ts[n - 1]) return [xs[n - 1], ys[n - 1]];
    var lo = 0, hi = n - 1;
    while (hi - lo > 1) {
      var mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
      if (ts[mid] <= t) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    var frac = (ts[hi] !== ts[lo]) ? (t - ts[lo]) / (ts[hi] - ts[lo]) : 0.0;
    return [xs[lo] + frac * (xs[hi] - xs[lo]), ys[lo] + frac * (ys[hi] - ys[lo])];
  }

  // Exact instantaneous speed from conservation of energy, rather than
  // differencing the (adaptively, unevenly spaced) simulated positions.
  function speedFromEnergy(energy, r) {
    var vsq = 2 * (energy + GM_SUN / r);
    return Math.sqrt(Math.max(0.0, vsq));
  }

  // A bound, uncrashed orbit is a closed ellipse retracing itself exactly
  // every period -- loop over one period for a seamless replay. A crashed
  // or escaping trajectory has no such periodicity, so it just replays its
  // finite simulated arc.
  function nLoopWindow(sim) {
    if (sim.bound && !sim.crashed) return Math.max(sim.period, 0.01);
    return Math.max(sim.ts[sim.ts.length - 1], 0.01);
  }

  // Approximation of matplotlib's "plasma" colormap.
  var PLASMA_STOPS = [
    [0.0, [13, 8, 135]], [0.1, [70, 3, 159]], [0.2, [114, 1, 168]],
    [0.3, [156, 23, 158]], [0.4, [189, 55, 134]], [0.5, [216, 87, 107]],
    [0.6, [237, 121, 83]], [0.7, [251, 159, 58]], [0.8, [253, 202, 38]],
    [0.9, [240, 249, 33]], [1.0, [240, 249, 33]]
  ];
  function plasma(t) {
    t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));
    for (var i = 0; i < PLASMA_STOPS.length - 1; i++) {
      var t0 = PLASMA_STOPS[i][0], t1 = PLASMA_STOPS[i + 1][0];
      if (t >= t0 && t <= t1) {
        var f = (t1 > t0) ? (t - t0) / (t1 - t0) : 0;
        var c0 = PLASMA_STOPS[i][1], c1 = PLASMA_STOPS[i + 1][1];
        var r = Math.round(c0[0] + (c1[0] - c0[0]) * f);
        var g = Math.round(c0[1] + (c1[1] - c0[1]) * f);
        var b = Math.round(c0[2] + (c1[2] - c0[2]) * f);
        return "rgb(" + r + "," + g + "," + b + ")";
      }
    }
    var last = PLASMA_STOPS[PLASMA_STOPS.length - 1][1];
    return "rgb(" + last[0] + "," + last[1] + "," + last[2] + ")";
  }

  var speedSlider = document.getElementById("new-speed");
  var speedVal = document.getElementById("new-speed-val");
  var angleSlider = document.getElementById("new-angle");
  var angleVal = document.getElementById("new-angle-val");
  var timeSlider = document.getElementById("new-time");
  var playBtn = document.getElementById("new-play");
  var summary = document.getElementById("new-summary");
  var canvas = document.getElementById("new-canvas");
  var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");

  var state = { sim: null };

  var PLOT_W = 500; // px, square plot region within the canvas
  var PLOT_PAD = 20;

  function render() {
    var sim = state.sim;
    var xs = sim.xs, ys = sim.ys, ts = sim.ts;
    var t = parseFloat(timeSlider.value);

    var loopMax = nLoopWindow(sim);
    if (sim.bound && !sim.crashed) {
      var cut = ts.length;
      for (var i = 0; i < ts.length; i++) { if (ts[i] > loopMax) { cut = i; break; } }
      cut = Math.max(cut, 2);
      xs = xs.slice(0, cut); ys = ys.slice(0, cut); ts = ts.slice(0, cut);
    }

    var pos = interpPosition(t, ts, xs, ys);
    var px = pos[0], py = pos[1];

    var speeds = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) speeds.push(speedFromEnergy(sim.energy, Math.hypot(xs[i], ys[i])));

    var vLo, vHi;
    if (sim.bound) {
      var vPeri = speedFromEnergy(sim.energy, sim.periapsis);
      var vApo = speedFromEnergy(sim.energy, sim.apoapsis);
      vLo = Math.min(vPeri, vApo); vHi = Math.max(vPeri, vApo);
    } else {
      vLo = Math.min.apply(null, speeds); vHi = Math.max.apply(null, speeds);
    }
    if (vHi - vLo < 1e-4) vHi = vLo + 1e-4;
    function norm(v) { return (v - vLo) / (vHi - vLo); }

    var absXs = xs.map(Math.abs), absYs = ys.map(Math.abs);
    var span = Math.max(Math.max.apply(null, absXs), Math.max.apply(null, absYs), R_START) * 1.15;
    function sx(x) { return PLOT_PAD + (x + span) / (2 * span) * PLOT_W; }
    function sy(y) { return PLOT_PAD + PLOT_W - (y + span) / (2 * span) * PLOT_W; }

    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
    ctx.fillStyle = "#fbfbf8";
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, PLOT_W + 2 * PLOT_PAD, PLOT_W + 2 * PLOT_PAD);

    var rCrashPx = R_CRASH / (2 * span) * PLOT_W;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(242,193,78,0.35)";
    ctx.arc(sx(0), sy(0), rCrashPx, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill();

    for (var i2 = 0; i2 < xs.length - 1; i2++) {
      var segSpeed = (speeds[i2] + speeds[i2 + 1]) / 2;
      ctx.strokeStyle = plasma(norm(segSpeed));
      ctx.lineWidth = 2.4;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(sx(xs[i2]), sy(ys[i2]));
      ctx.lineTo(sx(xs[i2 + 1]), sy(ys[i2 + 1]));
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#d99a2b";
    ctx.arc(sx(0), sy(0), 9, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill();

    var vHere = speedFromEnergy(sim.energy, Math.hypot(px, py));
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = plasma(norm(vHere));
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#ffffff";
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.6;
    ctx.arc(sx(px), sy(py), 6.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();

    // Colour bar -- speed scale, top = fastest (periapsis), bottom = slowest.
    var barX = PLOT_W + 2 * PLOT_PAD + 32, barY = 34, barW = 16, barH = canvas.height - 64;
    var grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, barY, 0, barY + barH);
    for (var gstep = 0; gstep <= 10; gstep++) grad.addColorStop(gstep / 10, plasma(1 - gstep / 10));
    ctx.fillStyle = grad;
    ctx.fillRect(barX, barY, barW, barH);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#999"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.strokeRect(barX, barY, barW, barH);
    ctx.fillStyle = "#333";
    ctx.font = "10px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif";
    ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText(vHi.toFixed(2), barX + barW + 4, barY + 8);
    ctx.fillText(vLo.toFixed(2), barX + barW + 4, barY + barH);
    ctx.fillText("Speed", barX - 4, barY - 20);
    ctx.fillText("(AU/yr)", barX - 4, barY - 8);

    timeSlider.value = t;

    var lines = [];
    if (sim.crashed) {
      lines.push("<strong>Crashed into the Sun</strong> at simulated time " +
        sim.ts[sim.ts.length - 1].toFixed(3) + " years -- not enough sideways speed " +
        "(or aimed too directly inward) to miss it.");
    } else if (!sim.bound) {
      lines.push("<strong>Escapes to infinity.</strong> This launch speed and angle give the " +
        "planet more energy than it needs to stay bound to the Sun at all -- it never comes back.");
    } else {
      var shape = sim.e < 0.01 ? "a circle" : "an ellipse";
      lines.push("<strong>Settles into " + shape + "</strong>" );
    }
    summary.innerHTML = lines.join("<br><br>");
  }

  var playing = false, timerId = null;
  function stop() {
    playing = false;
    if (timerId !== null) { clearInterval(timerId); timerId = null; }
  }
  function start() {
    playing = true;
    timerId = setInterval(function () {
      var loopMax = nLoopWindow(state.sim);
      var dt = loopMax / 60.0;
      var t = parseFloat(timeSlider.value) + dt;
      if (t >= loopMax) t = loopMax > 0 ? (t % loopMax) : 0.0;
      timeSlider.value = t;
      render();
    }, 150);
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener("click", function () { if (playing) stop(); else start(); });

  function recompute() {
    state.sim = runNewtonSim(parseFloat(speedSlider.value), parseFloat(angleSlider.value));
    var newMax = nLoopWindow(state.sim);
    timeSlider.max = newMax.toFixed(4);
    timeSlider.value = 0;
    render();
  }

  speedSlider.addEventListener("input", function () {
    speedVal.textContent = parseFloat(speedSlider.value).toFixed(2);
    recompute();
  });
  angleSlider.addEventListener("input", function () {
    angleVal.textContent = parseFloat(angleSlider.value).toFixed(0);
    recompute();
  });
  timeSlider.addEventListener("input", render);

  speedVal.textContent = parseFloat(speedSlider.value).toFixed(2);
  angleVal.textContent = parseFloat(angleSlider.value).toFixed(0);
  recompute();
})();
</script>
```
:::


To understand how the simulations work we need to go back to the discoveries of Galileo, Kepler and Newton. 

### 1. Galileo: evidence that not everything orbits the Earth

In 1610, Galileo discovered four moons orbiting Jupiter. Press play below and watch Jupiter's four largest moons complete their real orbital periods. Note that the inner-most moons orbit faster than the outer-most ones.

::: {#fig-galileo-moons .content-hidden when-format="pdf"}

<div id="gal-app">

    <label for="gal-day">Day: <strong id="gal-day-val">0.0</strong></label>

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  if (window.SHOW_JS_APPS === false) return;

  // Galileo's four moons of Jupiter: real orbital periods and relative
  // distances, each moving on a circular orbit seen edge-on (as Galileo
  // actually saw them, roughly in a line through Jupiter) -- that alone
  // reproduces what he sketched night after night in January 1610.
  var MOON_NAMES = ["Io", "Europa", "Ganymede", "Callisto"];
  var MOON_COLORS = ["#e07b39", "#c9a86a", "#8a8f98", "#5b7fae"];
  var MOON_PERIOD_DAYS = [1.769, 3.551, 7.155, 16.689];
  var MOON_DISTANCE = [5.9, 9.4, 15.0, 26.4]; // Jupiter radii
  var MOON_PHASE = [0.0, 1.9, 0.7, 4.4]; // arbitrary starting phases so the
                                          // four moons aren't stacked at t=0
  var GALILEO_MAX_DAYS = 20.0; // a bit past Callisto's period, so the whole
                                // pattern repeats visibly before it loops
  var TICK_DT = 0.22, TICK_MS = 150;

  function moonPositions(tDays) {
    var xs = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < MOON_NAMES.length; i++) {
      var phase = 2 * Math.PI * (tDays / MOON_PERIOD_DAYS[i]) + MOON_PHASE[i];
      xs.push(MOON_DISTANCE[i] * Math.sin(phase));
    }
    return xs;
  }

  var daySlider = document.getElementById("gal-day");
  var dayVal = document.getElementById("gal-day-val");
  var playBtn = document.getElementById("gal-play");
  var summary = document.getElementById("gal-summary");
  var canvas = document.getElementById("gal-canvas");
  var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");

  var maxDist = Math.max.apply(null, MOON_DISTANCE) * 1.15;
  var X_MIN = -maxDist, X_MAX = maxDist;
  var Y_MIN = -maxDist * 0.4, Y_MAX = maxDist * 0.4;

  function sx(x, W) { return (x - X_MIN) / (X_MAX - X_MIN) * W; }
  function sy(y, H) { return H - (y - Y_MIN) / (Y_MAX - Y_MIN) * H; }

  function render() {
    var t = parseFloat(daySlider.value);
    var W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;

    ctx.fillStyle = "#0d1b2a";
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

    ctx.strokeStyle = "#3a4a5c";
    ctx.lineWidth = 0.8;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(0, sy(0, H));
    ctx.lineTo(W, sy(0, H));
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#d99a2b";
    ctx.arc(sx(0, W), sy(0, H), 9, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill();

    var xs = moonPositions(t);
    ctx.font = "11px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif";
    ctx.textAlign = "center";
    for (var i = 0; i < MOON_NAMES.length; i++) {
      var px = sx(xs[i], W), py = sy(0, H);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.fillStyle = MOON_COLORS[i];
      ctx.arc(px, py, 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.fillStyle = MOON_COLORS[i];
      ctx.fillText(MOON_NAMES[i], px, py - 12);
    }

    ctx.fillStyle = "#cfd8dc";
    ctx.fillText("distance from Jupiter (Jupiter radii)", W / 2, H - 8);

    dayVal.textContent = t.toFixed(1);

    var lines = ["<strong>Day " + t.toFixed(1) + "</strong>"];
    for (var j = 0; j < MOON_NAMES.length; j++) {
      lines.push("&bull; " + MOON_NAMES[j] + ": orbits every <strong>" +
        MOON_PERIOD_DAYS[j].toFixed(2) + " days</strong>");
    }
    summary.innerHTML = lines.join("<br>");
  }

  var playing = false, timerId = null;
  function stop() {
    playing = false;
    if (timerId !== null) { clearInterval(timerId); timerId = null; }
  }
  function start() {
    playing = true;
    timerId = setInterval(function () {
      var t = parseFloat(daySlider.value) + TICK_DT;
      if (t >= GALILEO_MAX_DAYS) t = t % GALILEO_MAX_DAYS;
      daySlider.value = t;
      render();
    }, TICK_MS);
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener("click", function () { if (playing) stop(); else start(); });
  daySlider.addEventListener("input", render);

  render();
})();
</script>
```
:::

### 2. Kepler: ellipses, equal areas, and a hidden pattern

Johannes Kepler found that planets in the solar system do not move in perfect circles, nor at constant speed. He distilled the pattern into three laws: 
- orbits are **ellipses** with the Sun at one focus (not the centre); - a planet **sweeps out equal areas in equal times**, moving faster when close to the Sun and slower when far away; 
- the **square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the orbit's size** 

Below you can explore all three below with Mercury, Earth, Mars and Jupiter's real orbital data. Against note that inner-most planets orbit faster than outer-most ones.

::: {#fig-kepler-orbits .content-hidden when-format="pdf"}

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  if (window.SHOW_JS_APPS === false) return;

  // Kepler's three laws, worked out empirically -- so this section doesn't
  // simulate gravity at all: each planet is placed directly on an ellipse
  // (by solving Kepler's own equation for its position at time t), exactly
  // the way Kepler described it. Real, approximate values for four planets.
  var PLANET_NAMES = ["Mercury", "Earth", "Mars", "Jupiter"];
  var PLANET_COLORS = ["#8a8f98", "#2e7d32", "#c0392b", "#c77f00"];
  var PLANET_A = [0.387, 1.000, 1.524, 5.203]; // semi-major axis, AU
  var PLANET_E = [0.206, 0.017, 0.093, 0.049]; // eccentricity
  var PLANET_T = PLANET_A.map(function (a) { return Math.pow(a, 1.5); }); // Kepler's 3rd law
  var KEPLER_MAX_YEARS = 12.0; // a little past Jupiter's ~11.86-year period
  var TICK_DT = 0.085, TICK_MS = 100;

  function mod(a, n) { return ((a % n) + n) % n; }

  // Solve M = E - e*sin(E) for the eccentric anomaly E (Newton's method).
  // It's because E doesn't increase uniformly with time (only M does) that
  // a planet visibly speeds up and slows down around its orbit.
  function solveKeplerEquation(M, e) {
    var tol = 1e-10, maxIter = 50;
    M = mod(M, 2 * Math.PI);
    var E = e < 0.8 ? M : Math.PI;
    for (var i = 0; i < maxIter; i++) {
      var f = E - e * Math.sin(E) - M;
      var fp = 1 - e * Math.cos(E);
      var dE = f / fp;
      E -= dE;
      if (Math.abs(dE) < tol) break;
    }
    return E;
  }

  // Position at time t, Sun at the origin (a focus, not the centre) --
  // perihelion sits on the positive x-axis.
  function keplerPosition(t, a, e, period) {
    var M = 2 * Math.PI * mod(t, period) / period;
    var E = solveKeplerEquation(M, e);
    return [a * (Math.cos(E) - e), a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e) * Math.sin(E)];
  }

  function ellipseOutline(a, e, n) {
    n = n || 200;
    var pts = [];
    for (var i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
      var E = 2 * Math.PI * i / n;
      pts.push([a * (Math.cos(E) - e), a * Math.sqrt(1 - e * e) * Math.sin(E)]);
    }
    return pts;
  }

  // Area swept between t0 and t0+dt, by sampling the true (non-uniform
  // speed) path and summing the shoelace formula relative to the focus at
  // the origin -- a genuine numerical measurement, not an assumed answer.
  function sweptArea(t0, dt, a, e, period, k) {
    k = k || 300;
    var pts = [];
    for (var i = 0; i <= k; i++) pts.push(keplerPosition(t0 + dt * i / k, a, e, period));
    var area = 0.0;
    for (var i = 0; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
      area += pts[i][0] * pts[i + 1][1] - pts[i + 1][0] * pts[i][1];
    }
    return Math.abs(area) / 2.0;
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Main orbit view
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  var yearSlider = document.getElementById("kep-year");
  var yearVal = document.getElementById("kep-year-val");
  var playBtn = document.getElementById("kep-play");
  var mainSummary = document.getElementById("kep-summary");
  var mainCanvas = document.getElementById("kep-canvas");
  var mainCtx = mainCanvas.getContext("2d");

  var lim = PLANET_A[3] * (1 + PLANET_E[3]) * 1.1;

  function mainRender() {
    var t = parseFloat(yearSlider.value);
    var W = mainCanvas.width, H = mainCanvas.height;
    function sx(x) { return (x + lim) / (2 * lim) * W; }
    function sy(y) { return H - (y + lim) / (2 * lim) * H; }

    mainCtx.fillStyle = "#fbfbf8";
    mainCtx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

    mainCtx.beginPath();
    mainCtx.fillStyle = "#d99a2b";
    mainCtx.arc(sx(0), sy(0), 8, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    mainCtx.fill();

    mainCtx.font = "11px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif";
    for (var i = 0; i < PLANET_NAMES.length; i++) {
      var outline = ellipseOutline(PLANET_A[i], PLANET_E[i]);
      mainCtx.beginPath();
      mainCtx.strokeStyle = PLANET_COLORS[i];
      mainCtx.globalAlpha = 0.5;
      mainCtx.lineWidth = 1.0;
      for (var j = 0; j < outline.length; j++) {
        var px = sx(outline[j][0]), py = sy(outline[j][1]);
        if (j === 0) mainCtx.moveTo(px, py); else mainCtx.lineTo(px, py);
      }
      mainCtx.stroke();
      mainCtx.globalAlpha = 1.0;

      var pos = keplerPosition(t, PLANET_A[i], PLANET_E[i], PLANET_T[i]);
      var qx = sx(pos[0]), qy = sy(pos[1]);
      mainCtx.beginPath();
      mainCtx.fillStyle = PLANET_COLORS[i];
      mainCtx.arc(qx, qy, 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
      mainCtx.fill();
      mainCtx.textAlign = "left";
      mainCtx.fillText(PLANET_NAMES[i], qx + 8, qy + 4);
    }

    yearVal.textContent = t.toFixed(2);

    var lines = ["<strong>Year " + t.toFixed(2) + "</strong>"];
    for (var k = 0; k < PLANET_NAMES.length; k++) {
      lines.push("&bull; " + PLANET_NAMES[k] + ": a=" + PLANET_A[k].toFixed(2) +
        " AU, e=" + PLANET_E[k].toFixed(3) + ", period=" + PLANET_T[k].toFixed(2) + " yr");
    }
    mainSummary.innerHTML = lines.join("<br>");
  }

  var playing = false, timerId = null;
  function stop() {
    playing = false;
    if (timerId !== null) { clearInterval(timerId); timerId = null; }
  }
  function start() {
    playing = true;
    timerId = setInterval(function () {
      var t = parseFloat(yearSlider.value) + TICK_DT;
      if (t >= KEPLER_MAX_YEARS) t = t % KEPLER_MAX_YEARS;
      yearSlider.value = t;
      mainRender();
    }, TICK_MS);
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener("click", function () { if (playing) stop(); else start(); });
  yearSlider.addEventListener("input", mainRender);
  mainRender();

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Third-law table
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  var tableRows = ["<table><thead><tr><th>Planet</th><th>a (AU)</th><th>T (years)</th><th>T² / a³</th></tr></thead><tbody>"];
  for (var t3 = 0; t3 < PLANET_NAMES.length; t3++) {
    var a3 = PLANET_A[t3], T3 = PLANET_T[t3];
    tableRows.push("<tr><td>" + PLANET_NAMES[t3] + "</td><td>" + a3.toFixed(3) +
      "</td><td>" + T3.toFixed(3) + "</td><td>" + ((T3 * T3) / (a3 * a3 * a3)).toFixed(3) + "</td></tr>");
  }
  tableRows.push("</tbody></table>");
  document.getElementById("kep-third-law-table").innerHTML = tableRows.join("");

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Equal-areas sub-widget (Mercury)
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  var windowSlider = document.getElementById("kep-window");
  var windowVal = document.getElementById("kep-window-val");
  var areasSummary = document.getElementById("kep-areas-summary");
  var areasCanvas = document.getElementById("kep-areas-canvas");
  var areasCtx = areasCanvas.getContext("2d");

  var MERC_A = PLANET_A[0], MERC_E = PLANET_E[0], MERC_T = PLANET_T[0];

  function areasRender() {
    var windowFrac = parseFloat(windowSlider.value);
    windowVal.textContent = windowFrac.toFixed(2);
    var dt = windowFrac * MERC_T;
    var areaPeri = sweptArea(0.0, dt, MERC_A, MERC_E, MERC_T);
    var areaAph = sweptArea(MERC_T / 2, dt, MERC_A, MERC_E, MERC_T);
    var periPts = [], aphPts = [];
    for (var i = 0; i <= 100; i++) {
      periPts.push(keplerPosition(dt * i / 100, MERC_A, MERC_E, MERC_T));
      aphPts.push(keplerPosition(MERC_T / 2 + dt * i / 100, MERC_A, MERC_E, MERC_T));
    }

    var W = areasCanvas.width, H = areasCanvas.height;
    var alim = MERC_A * (1 + MERC_E) * 1.15;
    function sx(x) { return (x + alim) / (2 * alim) * W; }
    function sy(y) { return H - (y + alim) / (2 * alim) * H; }

    areasCtx.fillStyle = "#fbfbf8";
    areasCtx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

    var outline = ellipseOutline(MERC_A, MERC_E);
    areasCtx.beginPath();
    areasCtx.strokeStyle = "#8a8f98";
    areasCtx.globalAlpha = 0.6;
    areasCtx.lineWidth = 1.0;
    for (var j = 0; j < outline.length; j++) {
      var px = sx(outline[j][0]), py = sy(outline[j][1]);
      if (j === 0) areasCtx.moveTo(px, py); else areasCtx.lineTo(px, py);
    }
    areasCtx.stroke();
    areasCtx.globalAlpha = 1.0;

    function fillWedge(pts, color) {
      areasCtx.beginPath();
      areasCtx.moveTo(sx(0), sy(0));
      for (var i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) areasCtx.lineTo(sx(pts[i][0]), sy(pts[i][1]));
      areasCtx.lineTo(sx(0), sy(0));
      areasCtx.closePath();
      areasCtx.fillStyle = color;
      areasCtx.fill();
    }
    fillWedge(periPts, "rgba(21,101,192,0.45)");
    fillWedge(aphPts, "rgba(192,57,43,0.45)");

    areasCtx.beginPath();
    areasCtx.fillStyle = "#d99a2b";
    areasCtx.arc(sx(0), sy(0), 7, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    areasCtx.fill();

    areasCtx.font = "12px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif";
    areasCtx.textAlign = "left";
    areasCtx.fillStyle = "#1565c0";
    areasCtx.fillText("■ near perihelion", W - 155, 18);
    areasCtx.fillStyle = "#c0392b";
    areasCtx.fillText("■ near aphelion", W - 155, 36);

    var pctDiff = Math.abs(areaPeri - areaAph) / Math.max(areaPeri, areaAph) * 100;
    var lines = [
      "Area near perihelion: <strong>" + areaPeri.toFixed(5) + " AU²</strong>",
      "Area near aphelion: <strong>" + areaAph.toFixed(5) + " AU²</strong>",
      "Difference: <strong>" + pctDiff.toFixed(2) + "%</strong> (numerical sampling error, not a real difference) -- the same time window sweeps essentially the same area, even though the perihelion arc covers visibly more ground because Mercury is moving faster there."
    ];
    areasSummary.innerHTML = lines.join("<br><br>");
  }

  windowSlider.addEventListener("input", areasRender);
  areasRender();
})();
</script>
```
:::

### 3. Newton: why doesn't it just fall in?

Kepler described *what* orbits look like; Newton explained *why*. His law of universal gravitation says the Sun pulls every planet straight towards itself, with a force that falls off as the square of the distance -- and nothing more. So why doesn't that pull simply drag every planet straight into the Sun? The answer is **sideways motion**: a planet is always "falling" towards the Sun, but it is also always moving sideways fast enough to keep missing it. In the app at the top of the page, you control a planet's launch speed and direction directly. Aim it steeply inward without enough sideways speed, and it crashes. Give it enough sideways speed, and the very same gravity that would have pulled it in instead bends its path into a closed ellipse -- or, with enough speed, flings it away for good. The path is coloured by the planet's instantaneous speed -- watch it turn bright near the Sun and dark on the far side of an elliptical orbit, direct visual evidence of Kepler's second law: the planet moves fastest exactly where it's closest to the Sun.

### 4. Bonus -- Einstein: the ellipse itself slowly turns

Newton's theory predicts a perfectly closed ellipse, retraced forever. For most planets that is an excellent match to reality -- but not quite perfect. Mercury's orbit, observed over centuries, precesses: its ellipse itself slowly rotates, by about 43 arcseconds per century beyond what Newtonian gravity (accounting for the pull of the other planets) predicts. This tiny leftover puzzled astronomers for decades, until Einstein's general relativity explained it as a consequence of gravity being, at heart, curved spacetime rather than a force acting instantly at a distance. The demo below adds a simplified correction to gravity with the right qualitative shape (it is **not** the exact general-relativistic formula) and turns the dial up far beyond Mercury's real, tiny effect, so the precession becomes visible over a handful of orbits instead of centuries.

::: {#fig-einstein-precession .content-hidden when-format="pdf"}

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  if (window.SHOW_JS_APPS === false) return;

  // Newton's gravity, on its own, produces a closed ellipse that never
  // changes orientation -- a direct consequence of the force being exactly
  // proportional to 1/r^2. General relativity's leading correction falls
  // off faster than 1/r^2, and any such deviation makes the orbit fail to
  // close -- the whole ellipse slowly rotates instead, a real effect
  // called perihelion precession, first confirmed for Mercury.
  //
  // This demo does NOT use the exact Schwarzschild formula -- rather than
  // risk misstating a precise coefficient, it adds a clearly-labelled,
  // simplified extra pull with the right qualitative shape (falling off as
  // 1/r^4, scaling with angular momentum squared) and an honest
  // "exaggeration" slider, so a visitor sees the real MECHANISM without
  // being told this is a precise reproduction of general relativity.
  var GM_SUN = 4 * Math.PI * Math.PI;
  var R_START = 1.0;
  var R_CRASH = 0.10;
  var V_CIRC = Math.sqrt(GM_SUN / R_START);

  var GR_BASE_SPEED = 0.7; // x circular speed -- visibly eccentric but safe orbit
  var GR_BASE_ANGLE = 0.0;
  var GR_N_ORBITS = 6;

  var MERCURY_PRECESSION_ARCSEC_PER_CENTURY = 43.0; // the real, well-known value
  var EPS_MAX = 0.0018; // calibrated to stay well clear of the crash threshold
                         // while still giving a dramatic ~90 deg/orbit precession
  var MERCURY_PERIOD_YEARS = Math.pow(0.387, 1.5); // a=0.387 AU, Kepler's 3rd law

  function mod(a, n) { return ((a % n) + n) % n; }

  function initialState(speedFactor, angleDeg) {
    var speed = speedFactor * V_CIRC;
    var theta = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180;
    return [R_START, 0.0, speed * Math.sin(theta), speed * Math.cos(theta)];
  }

  function classifyOrbit(x0, y0, vx0, vy0) {
    var r0 = Math.hypot(x0, y0);
    var v0sq = vx0 * vx0 + vy0 * vy0;
    var energy = 0.5 * v0sq - GM_SUN / r0;
    var L = x0 * vy0 - y0 * vx0;
    var info = { energy: energy, L: L, bound: energy < 0 };
    if (energy < 0) {
      var a = -GM_SUN / (2 * energy);
      var eSq = Math.max(0.0, 1 - (L * L) / (GM_SUN * a));
      var e = Math.sqrt(eSq);
      info.a = a; info.e = e;
      info.period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(Math.pow(a, 3) / GM_SUN);
    }
    return info;
  }

  function mercuryPrecessionDegPerOrbit(mercuryPeriodYears) {
    var orbitsPerCentury = 100.0 / mercuryPeriodYears;
    var arcsecPerOrbit = MERCURY_PRECESSION_ARCSEC_PER_CENTURY / orbitsPerCentury;
    return arcsecPerOrbit / 3600.0;
  }

  // Same adaptive velocity-Verlet integration as Newton's section, with one
  // extra term added to the acceleration: epsilon*GM*L^2/r^4, directed (like
  // gravity) towards the Sun. epsilon=0 exactly reproduces Newton's fixed
  // ellipse.
  function simulateGrOrbit(epsilon) {
    var maxSteps = 20000, eta = 0.006;
    var s0 = initialState(GR_BASE_SPEED, GR_BASE_ANGLE);
    var info = classifyOrbit(s0[0], s0[1], s0[2], s0[3]);
    var basePeriod = info.period;
    var maxTime = GR_N_ORBITS * basePeriod * 1.5;

    var xs = [s0[0]], ys = [s0[1]], ts = [0.0];
    var x = s0[0], y = s0[1], vx = s0[2], vy = s0[3], t = 0.0, crashed = false;
    for (var st = 0; st < maxSteps; st++) {
      var r = Math.hypot(x, y);
      if (r < R_CRASH) { crashed = true; break; }
      var L = x * vy - y * vx;
      var extra = epsilon * GM_SUN * L * L / Math.pow(r, 4);
      var ax = -GM_SUN * x / Math.pow(r, 3) - extra * x / r;
      var ay = -GM_SUN * y / Math.pow(r, 3) - extra * y / r;
      var dt = eta * Math.pow(r, 1.5) / Math.sqrt(GM_SUN);
      dt = Math.min(dt, maxTime / 400.0);
      var vxh = vx + 0.5 * ax * dt;
      var vyh = vy + 0.5 * ay * dt;
      x = x + vxh * dt; y = y + vyh * dt; t += dt;
      var r2 = Math.hypot(x, y);
      if (r2 < R_CRASH) { crashed = true; xs.push(x); ys.push(y); ts.push(t); break; }
      var L2 = x * vyh - y * vxh;
      var extra2 = epsilon * GM_SUN * L2 * L2 / Math.pow(r2, 4);
      var ax2 = -GM_SUN * x / Math.pow(r2, 3) - extra2 * x / r2;
      var ay2 = -GM_SUN * y / Math.pow(r2, 3) - extra2 * y / r2;
      vx = vxh + 0.5 * ax2 * dt; vy = vyh + 0.5 * ay2 * dt;
      xs.push(x); ys.push(y); ts.push(t);
      if (t >= maxTime) break;
    }

    var rs = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) rs.push(Math.hypot(xs[i], ys[i]));
    var periEvents = [];
    for (var j = 1; j < rs.length - 1; j++) {
      if (rs[j - 1] > rs[j] && rs[j] < rs[j + 1]) periEvents.push([ts[j], Math.atan2(ys[j], xs[j])]);
    }

    var precessionPerOrbit = null;
    if (periEvents.length >= 2) {
      var angles = periEvents.map(function (p) { return p[1]; });
      var unwrapped = [angles[0]];
      for (var k = 1; k < angles.length; k++) {
        var prev = unwrapped[unwrapped.length - 1];
        var da = angles[k] - mod(prev, 2 * Math.PI);
        while (da < -Math.PI) da += 2 * Math.PI;
        while (da > Math.PI) da -= 2 * Math.PI;
        unwrapped.push(prev + da);
      }
      var total = unwrapped[unwrapped.length - 1] - unwrapped[0];
      precessionPerOrbit = (total / (unwrapped.length - 1)) * (180 / Math.PI);
    }

    return { xs: xs, ys: ys, ts: ts, crashed: crashed, basePeriod: basePeriod,
      periEvents: periEvents, precessionPerOrbit: precessionPerOrbit };
  }

  var strengthSlider = document.getElementById("ein-strength");
  var strengthVal = document.getElementById("ein-strength-val");
  var timeSlider = document.getElementById("ein-time");
  var playBtn = document.getElementById("ein-play");
  var summary = document.getElementById("ein-summary");
  var canvas = document.getElementById("ein-canvas");
  var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");

  var state = { sim: null };

  function interpPosition(t, ts, xs, ys) {
    var n = ts.length;
    if (t <= ts[0]) return [xs[0], ys[0]];
    if (t >= ts[n - 1]) return [xs[n - 1], ys[n - 1]];
    var lo = 0, hi = n - 1;
    while (hi - lo > 1) {
      var mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
      if (ts[mid] <= t) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    var frac = (ts[hi] !== ts[lo]) ? (t - ts[lo]) / (ts[hi] - ts[lo]) : 0.0;
    return [xs[lo] + frac * (xs[hi] - xs[lo]), ys[lo] + frac * (ys[hi] - ys[lo])];
  }

  function render() {
    var sim = state.sim;
    var xs = sim.xs, ys = sim.ys, ts = sim.ts;
    var t = parseFloat(timeSlider.value);
    var pos = interpPosition(t, ts, xs, ys);
    var px = pos[0], py = pos[1];

    var W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;
    var absXs = xs.map(Math.abs), absYs = ys.map(Math.abs);
    var span = Math.max(Math.max.apply(null, absXs), Math.max.apply(null, absYs)) * 1.1;
    function sx(x) { return (x + span) / (2 * span) * W; }
    function sy(y) { return H - (y + span) / (2 * span) * H; }

    ctx.fillStyle = "#fbfbf8";
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#d99a2b";
    ctx.arc(sx(0), sy(0), 8, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill();

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(123,45,142,0.6)";
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.0;
    for (var i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) {
      var qx = sx(xs[i]), qy = sy(ys[i]);
      if (i === 0) ctx.moveTo(qx, qy); else ctx.lineTo(qx, qy);
    }
    ctx.stroke();

    for (var j = 0; j < sim.periEvents.length; j++) {
      var pe = interpPosition(sim.periEvents[j][0], ts, xs, ys);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(46,125,50,0.8)";
      ctx.arc(sx(pe[0]), sy(pe[1]), 3.2, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
      ctx.fill();
    }

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.fillStyle = "#d81b60";
    ctx.strokeStyle = "#ffffff";
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.2;
    ctx.arc(sx(px), sy(py), 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
    ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();

    var lines = [];
    var strength = parseFloat(strengthSlider.value);
    if (sim.crashed) {
      lines.push("<strong>Crashed into the Sun</strong> -- this strength destabilised the orbit.");
    } else if (strength === 0) {
      lines.push("<strong>This is pure Newtonian gravity</strong> -- notice the ellipse does NOT " +
        "turn at all, orbit after orbit. Move the slider to add the simplified relativistic correction.");
    } else if (sim.precessionPerOrbit === null) {
      lines.push("Not enough completed orbits yet to measure precession.");
    } else {
      var pp = sim.precessionPerOrbit;
      lines.push("<strong>Measured precession: " + pp.toFixed(2) + "° per orbit</strong> " +
        "(the green dots mark each detected closest approach -- watch them march around the Sun).");
      var mercuryReal = mercuryPrecessionDegPerOrbit(MERCURY_PERIOD_YEARS);
      var ratio = Math.abs(pp) / mercuryReal;
      lines.push("The real Mercury effect is about <strong>" + mercuryReal.toFixed(6) +
        "° per orbit</strong> (43 arcseconds per century) -- this demo is exaggerated roughly <strong>" +
        Math.round(ratio).toLocaleString() + "x</strong> so it's visible over just a few orbits instead of centuries.");
    }
    summary.innerHTML = lines.join("<br><br>");
  }

  var playing = false, timerId = null;
  function stop() {
    playing = false;
    if (timerId !== null) { clearInterval(timerId); timerId = null; }
  }
  function start() {
    playing = true;
    timerId = setInterval(function () {
      var maxT = Math.max(state.sim.ts[state.sim.ts.length - 1], 0.01);
      var dt = maxT / 100.0;
      var t = parseFloat(timeSlider.value) + dt;
      if (t >= maxT) t = maxT > 0 ? (t % maxT) : 0.0;
      timeSlider.value = t;
      render();
    }, 160);
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener("click", function () { if (playing) stop(); else start(); });
  timeSlider.addEventListener("input", render);

  function recompute() {
    var epsilon = (parseFloat(strengthSlider.value) / 100.0) * EPS_MAX;
    state.sim = simulateGrOrbit(epsilon);
    var newMax = Math.max(state.sim.ts[state.sim.ts.length - 1], 0.01);
    timeSlider.max = newMax.toFixed(4);
    timeSlider.value = 0;
    render();
  }

  strengthSlider.addEventListener("input", function () {
    strengthVal.textContent = parseFloat(strengthSlider.value).toFixed(0);
    recompute();
  });

  strengthVal.textContent = parseFloat(strengthSlider.value).toFixed(0);
  recompute();
})();
</script>
```
:::

A note on accuracy: sections 1-3 use real orbital data and exact physics -- the Galilean moons' real periods, the four planets' real semi-major axes and eccentricities, and an honest numerical simulation of Newton's law of gravity (the same simulation used to classify every orbit as crashing, elliptical, or escaping, and to measure the equal-areas result directly rather than assume it). Section 4's relativistic correction is deliberately simplified and exaggerated for visibility -- it has the right qualitative behaviour (it explains why the orbit precesses at all) but is not the precise Schwarzschild correction, and the demo says so directly rather than presenting the exaggerated numbers as Mercury's real effect.

:::
